title: U.S. House · California's 30th District
area: Burbank and Glendale, the Linda Vista neighborhood of Pasadena, and Los Angeles communities including parts of Hollywood, in Los Angeles County. District lines were redrawn for the 2026 election under California Proposition 50.

context.text: California redrew its congressional district lines for the 2026 election cycle after voters approved Proposition 50 on November 4, 2025, a mid-decade redistricting measure.

Incumbent Democrat Laura Friedman, first elected in 2024 to succeed Adam Schiff (who was elected to the U.S. Senate), and Republican Scott Meyers, an attorney, advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary.

summary.text: Laura Friedman is the Democratic incumbent for California's 30th Congressional District, first elected in 2024 to succeed Adam Schiff. She worked in film and television development and ran a small business before serving on the Glendale City Council and as mayor, then in the California State Assembly from 2016 to 2024. In the House she serves on the Transportation and Infrastructure and Science, Space, and Technology committees.

background.text: Born in New York; her official biography says she has lived in California for more than three decades and lives in Glendale with her husband and daughter.
Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Rochester in 1988.

Worked as a producer and head of development in the entertainment industry (her official biography describes a start as a film and television producer) and as a small-business owner selling antiques and decorative arts.
Served on the Glendale Design Review Board, was elected to the Glendale City Council in 2009 and re-elected in 2013, and served as mayor of Glendale from 2011 to 2012.

Served on the board of the Metropolitan Water District of Southern California, as a board member of the Southern California Association of Governments, and as past president of the Independent Cities Association.
Served in the California State Assembly from 2016 to 2024, representing the 43rd and later the 44th District.

In the Assembly she chaired the Transportation Committee and the Natural Resources Committee, served as Assistant Speaker pro Tempore, and chaired the Joint Rules Subcommittee on Sexual Harassment Prevention and Response; her official biography says she secured more than $60 million for local projects.
Was elected to the U.S. House in 2024 and took office in January 2025; serves on the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee and the Science, Space, and Technology Committee.

According to her official biography, the district includes Burbank, Glendale, West Hollywood, and parts of Los Angeles and Pasadena, and her stated focus areas are housing affordability, clean water, and protection from wildfires and other disasters.

priorities.text: Says she is committed to making housing affordable and helping more families become homeowners, and is co-leading House Democrats' Housing Affordability Working Group.
Says she will keep fighting to extend Affordable Care Act premium tax credits and protect affordable coverage for constituents.

positions.summary: Co-led the RELIEF Act to require automatic refunds to small businesses for tariffs the Trump administration collected, after the Supreme Court found the tariffs illegal.
positions.quote: The Supreme Court finally ruled what we all knew to be true: these tariff taxes are illegal. Over the past year, President Trump has cost families $1,200 and forced small businesses to pay roughly $200 billion in tariffs – now it’s time for the President to pay them back.

positions.summary: Backed House passage of legislation to extend Affordable Care Act premium tax credits, saying it would make healthcare more affordable and expand access to coverage.
positions.quote: This bill means more affordable healthcare, better access to care, and less financial strain for hardworking families. I’ll keep fighting to get it signed into law.

positions.summary: Cosponsored H.R. 3115, the Assault Weapons Ban of 2025, and H.R. 18, the Bipartisan Background Checks Act of 2025 (119th Congress).
Cosponsored H.R. 7346, the Drain ICE Act of 2026, which would remove funding for U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement from the 2025 reconciliation law (119th Congress).

Cosponsored H.R. 10600, the Abortion is Health Care Everywhere Act of 2026, and H.R. 4876, the Reproductive Freedom for Veterans Act, which directs the Department of Veterans Affairs to provide abortion care (119th Congress).
Cosponsored H.R. 2743, the Raise the Wage Act of 2025 (119th Congress).
Cosponsored H.Con.Res. 38 (Iran) and H.Con.Res. 68 (Venezuela), each directing the removal of U.S. Armed Forces from hostilities that Congress has not authorized (119th Congress).
Cosponsored H.R. 8085, the Ultra-Millionaire Tax Act of 2026, which imposes a tax on the net value of taxpayers' assets (119th Congress).

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure (Economic Development, Public Buildings and Emergency Management Subcommittee; Highways and Transit Subcommittee; Railroads, Pipelines and Hazardous Materials Subcommittee; Water Resources and Environment Subcommittee) and the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology (Energy Subcommittee) in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).
Original cosponsor of the RELIEF Act, which would require refunds of tariffs collected since January 1, 2025 that were found illegal by the Supreme Court.
Co-convened the first meeting of House Democrats' Housing Affordability Working Group with Rep. Emilia Sykes.

summary.text: Scott Meyers is the Republican nominee for California's 30th Congressional District. A California native and attorney, he describes himself as a small-business owner who has run his own law practice for about three decades and as not a career politician. He advanced from the June 2, 2026 primary.

background.text: Describes himself as a California native who has lived in the region for almost 50 years, raised by a schoolteacher and a minister, and who started working at age 14.
Graduated from Simi Valley High School and earned a law degree from Pepperdine University School of Law in 1988; his Ivoterguide profile also lists a bachelor's degree from UCLA.
According to his Ivoterguide profile, worked as an attorney at the firm Gilbert, Kelly Crowley & Jennett from 1988 to 1994 and at the Auto Club of Southern California from 1995 to 1999.
Has run the Law Offices of Scott A. Meyers since 2000, according to his Ivoterguide profile; he describes himself as self-employed for 26 years and a small business owner for three decades.

His Ivoterguide profile lists this race as the only office he has sought and reports no political offices held; he finished second in the June 2, 2026 top-two primary, advancing to the general election.

priorities.text: Lists three key campaign messages: full accountability and transparency over how tax money is spent; keeping "boys out of girls sports, and out of their locker rooms"; and full access to constituents through quarterly, open, unscripted press conferences.
Says he wants to "fight to bring film and television production back" to the district, which he calls "the entertainment capital of the world."

positions.summary: Campaign website says he supports legislation like the SAVE Act.
positions.quote: Support legislation like the SAVE Act to ensure confidence in our elections.

statements.quote: Oppose sanctuary policies that undermine public safety
Support law enforcement and restore consequences for crime
Fight for lower taxes and pro-growth policies

researchNotes: Laura Friedman has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey; positions and priorities were drawn from her official House issues page and press releases. Her federal floor votes and FEC totals are added separately by script. Scott Meyers completed the 2026 survey, which is the basis for his priorities and the tax position listed here. Scott Meyers: campaign website home and Issues pages added; the SAVE Act statement is the only direct match to a fixed issue statement. Biography expansion: Friedman's biography draws on her official House page and Ballotpedia; Scott Meyers has no official or news biography found, so his biography relies on Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey and his candidate-reported Ivoterguide profile (undergraduate degree and employers are from Ivoterguide only).
